pr_title: limit the allocator bitmap to 65536 bits
pr_body:
When creating 10K service using  a service subnet with a /12 mask, 
etcd runs out of space and the cluster needs manual intervention to
recover.

The service subnet uses a bitmap stored in etcd. Using a /12 subnet
imply that this bitmap can use 2^20 bits, something unnecessary
since Kubernetes is not validating more than 10K services.

We were already capping the bitmap to 2^16 bits for IPv6, this
just do the same for IPv4 subnets.

We still allow to configure /12 as subnet mask, but it won't be possible
to use IPs out of the lower 16 bits.


/kind bug

/kind failing-test

```release-note
the service IP allocator only allows to assign ClusterIPs in the lower 16 bits of the Service Subnet configured, despite it can have a maximum subnet mask of 20 bits (/12). This is the same behavior used for IPv6
```

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94029
Related KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1881

This looks like a breaking change, and a silently breaking one at that.

>> however, those users are the ones that will have etcd database sizes with ~2GB on bitmaps just because of the revisions stored in etcd...
>
> This isn't true. Compaction is happening every 5m by default, so if you are not creating hunderds/thousands of services in short periods of time, your fine.

* tracking written bytes (via any object) and compacting earlier if a threshold is exceeded
* monitoring etcd alarms and compacting based on that

2. Can the apiserver process the error  `etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded` and try a compaction, not waiting for the periodic compaction?
3. How the compact operations that should solve the problem fails with an error `database space exceeded` ?

The compactor in the apiserver needs to persist key `compact_rev_key` before requesting compaction [1]. That explains why it fails to compact etcd when etcd already reaches its backend quota limit.

When etcd server raises no space alarm, usually we need to perform:
1. compact the key space
2. defrag etcd backend
3. disarm the alarm

IIUC, the compactor in the apiserver is not designed to perform all these steps. So manual intervention or some other automated script is needed.

I have one suspect, I think that is caused by the bitmap used to store the cluster ips, under the key `/registry/ranges/serviceips`, related discussion here https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1881#issuecomment-671758404

I don't know how to get the size of the key value, so I did the following

```
root@kind-control-plane:~# ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt get /registry/ranges/serviceips > serviceips.bin                                                           
root@kind-control-plane:~# ls -alh serviceips.bin
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 129K Aug 17 22:28 serviceips.bin
```

the result seems correct, because I have configured a /12 range `10.96.0.0/12` for the service IP that is a 2^20 bitmap.

Each new service will create a new revision of that key to update the bitmap.

IIUC how etcd works, 129k per the 10000 services, if no compaction runs during that time, can be a a lot of space.

When the database space is exceeded, the health check start to restart etcd and the compactor can not persist the key as explained here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94029#issuecomment-674494952

If the compactor runs before the database space is exceeded there is no problem, and the cluster works

> 1. Is it possible that the health check don't act on the alarm `alarm:NOSPACE `, restarting etcd?  Restarting etcd makes the situation worse and it may miss a peridoc apiserver compaction.

I agree that restarting etcd does not help in this case. And I suspect that, in general, it's better to not restart etcd due to health check failures, but I don't have the data to prove that, so I'm hesitant to suggest disabling the liveness probe.  I'd be very interesting in data anyone is able to gather about this.

> 2. Can the apiserver process the error  `etcdserver: mvcc: database space exceeded` and try a compaction, not waiting for the periodic compaction?

This might be best to discuss at etcd.io/etcd and not at kubernetes/kubernetes, but etcd _compaction_ doesn't actually reduce the storage file size, it just frees pages within it for reuse. _defragmentation_ is the etcd operation that reduces the storage file size.  My preference would be we teach etcd to perform defragmentation automatically rather than waiting for an administrator to request it. I think etcd is much better positioned than the apiserver to decide when to do defragmentation, so I'd rather invest in improving etcd.

> 3. How the compact operations that should solve the problem fails with an error `database space exceeded` ?

See above about difference between _compaction_ and _defragmentation_.

I think this problem should be solved by `kube-apiserve`r. After all, when etcd database is full, etcdctl can compress it. K8s' etcd is only used by `kube-apiserver`, so `kube-apiserver` should handle this problem.

https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/14595#issuecomment-2449419446

Clarification, I think the issue with K8s getting stuck on `database space exceeded` is not because of etcd, but due to how K8s handles deletes and compaction. On pure etcd are still able to delete, compact to reduce size of database in use, and then defrag and disarm alarm to unlock writes. The improvements to compaction were discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/80513
